nodes.title: 🖼️ 3. Reference Images
widgets_values:
### Face Reference
- Use **close-up images** with the subject looking **directly at the camera**.  
- Prefer **neutral facial expressions** — avoid smiles or exaggerated expressions.  
- The clearer and more frontal the face, the better the swap alignment.

### Body Reference
- Avoid images where the person is **too far from the camera**; distant faces are harder to detect.  
- Avoid images with **multiple people**, unless you manually mask the correct target.  
- Use well-lit, natural environments whenever possible.

### Matching Tips
For best results:
- Choose **face and body references** with **similar skin tones** — this helps the lighting and tone blending look natural.  
- Try to match **face shapes** (e.g., round, oval, angular) between both images.  
  This ensures a more realistic fusion and avoids distortions around the jawline and cheeks.

nodes.title: 🎭 4. Masks
widgets_values:
### Important Notes
- For **head swaps**, enable segmentation of both **face and hair** in the node **“Body Reference Face Segmentation.”**  
- For **face-only swaps**, enable only the **face segmentation.**

### Common Mask Issues
- If parts of the face are obscured (e.g., a hand over the mouth or eyes), segmentation may fail to cover small regions such as gaps between fingers.  
  - To fix this, increase the `fill_holes` parameter in the **Mask Fix** node.  
  - Alternatively, refine the mask manually.

nodes.title: ⚙️ 2. Controls & Resolution
widgets_values:
* **Recommended Base Resolution:** `1328 × 1328`
  Avoid changing this value to maintain optimal compatibility with the model’s architecture and latent scaling.

* **Sampler & Scheduler ([RES4LYF](https://github.com/ClownsharkBatwing/RES4LYF)):**

  * **Sampler:** `res_2s`
  * **Scheduler:** `beta57`
  * **Steps:** 4 (default)

    * Sometimes, **3 steps** gives results closer to the reference face, though it may occasionally produce incomplete generations.

* **Mask Color:**
  Use **magenta (`221, 59, 207`)** as the mask color.
  This color is rarely present in images and works reliably with the inpainting prompt logic.

* **Inpainting Mode (Optional):**
  When **inpainting mode** is enabled, a **face-region mask** is automatically generated and used for a more concentrated editing process.
  This is useful when the body image has a **face that appears distant or lacks detail**, as the model will **zoom in and focus specifically on the masked region**, enhancing fine details such as facial structure and alignment.
  The process replaces only the masked portion and then **blends (pastes) it back** onto the final image.
  However, because the model works exclusively within the masked area, **poor or incomplete masks** — such as those that are too small, have holes, or fail to fully cover the target face — will lead to **distorted or low-quality results**.
  If **inpainting mode** is disabled, the generation relies solely on the **reference images, prompt, and the head-swap LoRA**, without using any mask-based refinement.
Enable painting mode (recommended for images where the face is very far away, it increases the quality in general but can generate incomplete faces if the mask is not accurate)

nodes.title: Prompt LLM
widgets_values:
Describe the person’s overall facial appearance, gender presentation (male or female), head shape, and any visible accessories as seen in the image. Include details such as the overall head size and proportions, facial structure (shape of the face, jawline, chin type, and cheekbones), expression, and skin texture. Describe hair characteristics including color, length, texture, and general style. If visible, mention accessories like piercings, glasses, or earrings, but only if they clearly appear in the image — do not invent or assume any. Do not describe clothing, hats, or the background. Focus strictly on the natural head, face, hair, and visible facial accessories present in the image.

Expected answer examples:

1. Female with an oval head and balanced proportions, fair skin, straight medium-length blonde hair, and small silver nose piercing.
2. Male with a round head and wide jaw, tan skin, short curly black hair (no long hair or braids), wearing black-framed glasses.
3. Female with an angular face, defined cheekbones, pointed chin, olive skin, wavy shoulder-length brown hair (no short or pixie cut), and no accessories.
4. Female with a heart-shaped face, narrow chin, warm undertones, long straight red hair (no curls or short styles), and gold hoop earrings.
5. Male with a square jawline, medium brown skin, short textured dark hair (no long hair or ponytail), and small lip piercing.
6. Female with a narrow head, pale skin, medium wavy gray hair (no long straight hair), and thin metal eyeglasses.
7. Male with a diamond-shaped face, high cheekbones, light skin, short black textured hair (no long hair, no braids), and eyebrow piercing.
8. Male with a rectangular head, strong jawline, medium tan skin, short slicked-back brown hair (no long hair or side braids), and no accessories.
9. Female with a long face, fair skin, straight light brown hair (no curls or short cuts), transparent glasses, and slightly small chin.
10. Male with a round head, dark skin, short afro hair (no dreadlocks, no long hair), and small gold stud earrings.

nodes.title: 🔧 5. Core Processing
widgets_values:
### Pose Map Influence
The **pose map** can improve the match between the body and face orientation.  
However:
- It sometimes alters facial proportions (eye spacing, jawline, etc.), making the result less faithful to the face reference.
- If the resemblance decreases, **disconnect the “pose_map” input** from the **Qwen Text Encode Custom** node.

A reroute node is placed in front of the input for easy disconnection when needed.

> 💡 Tip: Use pose maps only when both the face and body reference are similar in orientation and lighting.

---

### Ollama Describer Integration
This workflow includes the **Ollama Describer** node, which extracts facial expression and pose details from the body reference image.  
These details are used to dynamically enrich the prompt for Qwen, enhancing realism and consistency.

You can replace this with any node capable of analyzing an image and generating textual descriptions (e.g., Qwen-VL, Gemini, Florence2, etc.).

---

### Inpainting Strategy
The inpainting method applies generation **only inside the masked region**, preserving all other image areas untouched.  
This ensures the rest of the image (environment, lighting, etc.) remains consistent with the original body reference.

Auxiliary nodes like:
- **Reference Latent**
- **Differential Diffusion**

…help maintain local detail consistency and improve blending quality.

---

### Troubleshooting Tips
If the result looks off:
1. Change the **seed** and re-generate.  
2. Try toggling the **pose map** on/off.  
3. As a last resort, use the **Planar Face Overlay** masks and outputs.

---

If you want the pose map to be used, you can remove bypass. This makes it follow the pose of the face elements more closely, but it can make it less similar to the reference image of the face, as it will influence the distance between the eyes and between the nose and mouth, changing the physiognomy, as well as having a greater chance of generating a more plasticized texture.
